full_zh: 背景：还是同一个项目。我的第一反应是把所有事都交给代理，包括数数和修小的评审意见。
目标：找出哪些地方让代理做反而花得比省得多。
我做了什么，第一步是计数：切分线、覆盖率百分比、正文里的「N 道题」，手工数曾经错过两次。所以现在每个计数都由脚本产生，模型永远不数数。
第二步是小修：一轮代理修订实测要 5 到 6 分钟、多 4 万到 6 万 token，所以一行的修改我就地改，只有实质性修改才回到代理。第三步是并行度：一个问题一个代理浪费上下文，一次性开四个代理又破了上限，最后定为每个代理两道题、同时三个代理。后来我的 Amazon 备考覆盖矩阵也改成由脚本从一份映射生成，不会漂移。
结果与学到：审阅一对完成的题只需要三到六次工具调用，用的是脚本而不是模型。模型用在输出开放且可检查的地方，答案确定的地方，写十行代码。
full_en: Same build. My first instinct was to hand everything to an agent, including counting things and fixing small review comments, and I wanted to find where that actually cost more than it saved. First, counts. Cut lines, coverage percentages and the N problems in prose had been wrong by hand, twice, so now every count comes from a script and a model never counts. Second, small fixes. An agent revision round measured five to six minutes and forty to sixty thousand extra tokens, so a one-line fix I edit in place, and the agent round trip is for substantive changes. Third, parallelism. One agent per problem wasted context, and four agents just this once broke my cap, so I settled on two problems per agent, three agents at a time. Later, my Amazon-prep coverage matrix is generated by a script from one mapping, so it cannot drift. Now reviewing a finished pair takes three to six tool calls, using a script, not a model. I use a model where the output is open-ended and checkable. Where the answer is deterministic, I write ten lines of code.

full.example: Handing counting to an agent cost more than it saved.
Where the answer is deterministic, I write ten lines of code.
The coverage matrix is generated from a single source of truth, so it cannot drift.

starl.example: A one-line fix is not worth an agent round trip.
I right-sized the work to two problems per agent.
Delegation has overhead in context and tokens.

followups.example: I play to the model's strengths: open-ended, checkable output.

followups.zh: 默认先用最便宜的工具
followups.example: I default to the cheapest tool that gives a verifiable answer.
Two problems per agent was the sweet spot.

senior.q: How do you decide, in the moment, whether a task is worth delegating to an agent?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你有没有可复用的判断框架，而不是凭感觉。
framework: 先问答案是否确定：确定则用脚本
再问改动大小：一行就地改，实质改动回到同一个有上下文的代理
最后问有没有可执行的验收：没有就先写验收再委派
senior.best_practice: 委派有成本，包括等待、上下文和审查。三个问题依次过滤，能把大多数不划算的委派挡在门外。先问最便宜的问题，决策本身也省时间。

terms.example: I use a three-question decision rule before delegating.
A back-of-envelope cost check usually settles it.

senior.q: How would you measure whether the time and tokens saved are real, and not just your impression?
senior.why: 面试官在探：Frugality 要用数据，而不是印象。
framework: 先说记录基线：一轮修订的耗时和 token 数是实测出来的
再说对比两条路径：脚本或就地修改与代理往返的总成本
最后说持续追踪：把几个关键数字定期复查，看规则是否仍然成立
senior.best_practice: 节省必须用同一把尺子量两条路径。我之所以有 5 到 6 分钟这类数字，是因为测过。没有基线的节省只是印象，面试官会追问数据。

terms.example: I measured a baseline for one revision round before deciding.
I compared the two paths apples to apples.

senior.q: As models get cheaper and faster, does your rule about not delegating small fixes still hold?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你的原则是否随条件变化而更新，而不是教条。
framework: 先说规则背后的原因是成本和确定性，不是对模型的偏见
再说随成本下降，阈值会移动：更多小任务会变得值得委派
但确定性问题仍然应该用脚本，因为脚本给的是 oracle，模型给的是看起来合理的答案
senior.best_practice: 好的规则要说明它依赖的前提。成本类前提会变，所以阈值要定期复核；确定性类前提不会变，所以计数永远交给脚本。区分这两类前提，说明你理解规则而不是背规则。

terms.example: I'd revisit the threshold as costs change.
I reason from first principles, not from a fixed rule.

senior.q: How would you teach a team to avoid over-delegating to AI without discouraging adoption?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你能否在推广 AI 和控制成本之间平衡。
framework: 先肯定采用：目标是用在对的地方，而不是少用
再给出一页简单的判断表和几个对照例子，让大家看到差别
最后放进共享的模板或指令里，而不是靠说教
senior.best_practice: 推广 AI 时反对滥用的最好方式是给判断标准和真实例子，而不是禁止。把标准固化进共享文件，团队不用每次重新讨论，也不会觉得被否定。

terms.example: I frame it as guardrails, not gates.
I lead by example with concrete cases from my own build.
